releases.title: Results site before the review-driven redesign

changes.text: FMAM 2026 March, April and May verified against official CHIRPS v2.0 observations.
ONDJ shown on the ONDJ R3 (Deyr) rainfall domain (575 cells) instead of the earlier >=120 mm / 20% rule.

releases.title: Redesign around the reader: one cycle selector, outlook first, verification narrative

changes.text: Cycle and area selectors drive every section; shareable view links; outlook and map first; status panel with precise target statuses; verification narrative and paired anomaly chart; per-cycle CSV downloads.

releases.title: Area-specific historical skill and clearer uncertainty

changes.text: Historical skill computed for each cycle's rainfall domain and the R0-R3 regions from stored cross-validated probabilities (no refitting).

Skill labels reflect intervals and Holm-adjusted p-values; verification narrative always reports the rainfall error; climatology defined as observed tercile frequencies; unavailable verification explained; separate verification panels.

releases.title: Historical verification explorer, forecast-and-evidence package, map comparison and release archive

changes.text: Historical diagnostics per cycle, target and area: performance by year, reliability diagrams, probability histograms and category Brier skill (cross-validated and exploratory).

PDF bulletin and one-click ZIP package per cycle; side-by-side forecast vs observed anomaly maps; release archive and change log; research label on phones; keyboard focus kept when leaving an unavailable view.

releases.title: Comparison with official outlooks (ICPAC OND 2026 update, EMI Bega 2026/27)

changes.text: New pipeline: ICPAC and EMI products discovered, downloaded and versioned by content hash; standardized records; comparison with the native ONDJ forecast; rule-based interpretation. Comparison numbers are published only after a person reviews the extracted values.
Outlooks section shows the official figures, the providers' own text, source records and the status of each comparison; ONDJ gallery links the review report.

releases.title: Reviewed comparison with official outlooks published

changes.text: EMI zone values and the digitized ICPAC map were reviewed by the project team; the comparison findings, numbers and maps are now published (agreement in the south and south-east, disagreement in EMI zone III).

releases.title: Clearer, scoped comparison with official outlooks; review and publication safeguards

changes.text: Comparison follows the selected area (season scope stated for monthly targets); key findings, maps and compact tables first; agreement shares always with their compared area; clickable evidence; comparison downloads and package files; 'Compare outlooks' in the navigation; archived comparison pages repaired.

Bounded sensitivity checks (EMI neighbourhood size and arrow position, ICPAC registration by one pixel); tie-aware favoured category; reviews bound to the extracted contents; publication withheld when the saved comparison no longer matches its inputs.

releases.title: Comparison reports and scope details corrected

changes.text: Public and packaged comparison reports generated from the published (reviewed, current) data only; report figures resolve inside the ZIP; EMI samples labelled by their overlap with the domain; evidence maps follow each finding's scope; publication check includes the favoured-category threshold and the saved source manifest.

releases.title: EMI figure beside the platform map; ICPAC comparison table

changes.text: The platform map with EMI zone values is shown next to EMI's official ONDJ 2026/27 figure; a new ICPAC table gives ICPAC's printed favoured category and interval against the platform's below/near/above probabilities at the sampled locations and for each area.

releases.title: EMI zones as homogeneous rainfall regions (digitized, pending review)

changes.text: EMI homogeneous rainfall regions I-VIII digitized from Korecha and Sorteberg (2013, doi:10.1002/2013WR013760) as a reviewable reference layer; once reviewed, the comparison adds platform means over each whole EMI zone and a redrawn region map with EMI's 2026/27 values beside the platform map. Region boundaries drawn on the platform map.

releases.title: Reviewed EMI rainfall regions published

changes.text: The digitized EMI homogeneous rainfall regions were reviewed by the project team; the site now shows the redrawn region map with EMI's 2026/27 values beside the platform map, region lines on the platform map, and platform means over each whole EMI zone (zone III opposing, VI-VIII agreeing on above normal).

releases.title: Comparison pipeline ready for other seasons

changes.text: Map titles and table notes use each season's own labels and months; zone tables hide arrow columns for seasons whose EMI zones have no arrows. ONDJ results unchanged.

releases.title: FMAM 2026 verified; February initialization; FMAM rainfall contribution domain; outlooks scored against CHIRPS

changes.text: February 2026 and the full FMAM 2026 season verified for both initializations. CHIRPS never published the February by_month file; February is taken from the official annual p25 file after checking it is identical to the published by_month files of January and March 2026.

Main FMAM area: the FMAM rainfall contribution domain (FMAM >= 100 mm and >= 20% of annual rainfall, CHIRPS 1993-2025), replacing the earlier R2-based domain; the FMAM main-season domain (>= 40% of annual) is a second view. The earlier R2-based verification report is archived as superseded.

The platform, EMI and ICPAC are scored against CHIRPS for each one's own period (single season): favoured-category matches with observation, outlook and favoured-category coverage, and RPSS for the platform and EMI. Observed CHIRPS terciles are shown alongside the three outlooks. Comparison results are computed separately for every domain view.

Verification reports state the cycle's own initialization and season; one current report per cycle. Comparison maps draw the national border once. Historical performance opens with a takeaway; technical detail is expandable.

releases.title: Climatology and domain reviews for JJAS and ONDJ; historical rainfall-amount skill for FMAM and ONDJ

changes.text: Rainfall climatology and domain reviews for JJAS (with EMI's Kiremt 2026 long-term maps 2(e) and 3(e), digitization in draft) and ONDJ (no EMI long-term Bega maps published yet). Evidence only: the JJAS R1+R2 and ONDJ R3 domains are unchanged.

Calibration development runs (fit 1993-2016, evaluate 2017 onwards) for both FMAM initializations and ONDJ, so Historical performance now shows rainfall-amount skill for every cycle (all of Ethiopia): FMAM CRPSS -0.001 (January) and +0.053 (February), ONDJ +0.18 (2017-2024), JJAS +0.017.
The Rainfall climatology and domains section shows the selected season's review; comparison notes and map captions name each cycle's own periods and seasons.

releases.title: CHIRPS v3.0 adopted: every cycle recalibrated and re-verified (2026 forecasts retrospective)

changes.text: Observations changed from CHIRPS v2.0 (daily p25) to CHIRPS v3.0 (official monthly 0.05 degree product averaged onto the 0.25 degree grid; Funk et al. 2026). The whole chain was refitted with the same method: amount correction, terciles, blend weights, historical evaluation, development runs and decision gates (which give the same outcome as with v2.0).

The 2026 forecasts of all four cycles were recalibrated with CHIRPS v3.0 after their outcomes were known and are verified against CHIRPS v3.0 (FMAM Feb-May and season, JJAS Jun-Aug). They are retrospective reconstructions; the CHIRPS v2.0 versions are release 2026-10-10.2.

The FMAM rainfall contribution domain keeps its rule (FMAM >= 100 mm and >= 20% of annual) on the CHIRPS v3.0 climatology: 75.6% of Ethiopia (72.6% with v2.0). The JJAS R1+R2 and ONDJ R3 regime domains are unchanged; the regimes come from the CHIRPS v2.0 daily climatology.
The v2.0 vs v3.0 comparison (climatology about 15% wetter with v3.0, seasonal shares and year rankings closely agreeing; calibration skill similar overall) is in Methods and docs/45.

releases.title: Smoother maps (display only)

changes.text: Map display smoothing raised from 0.6 to 1.5 native cells (about 0.38 degrees), which softens the 1-degree steps the forecasts inherit from the ECMWF model grid; rainfall-domain edges are smoothed within the country instead of following the 0.25-degree mask cells. Forecast values, statistics, verification and exported files are unchanged (native 0.25-degree grid).

releases.title: Grid-cell map style (0.25°)

changes.text: Forecast maps can be shown as Smoothed (default) or Grid cells (0.25°): every cell drawn exactly as computed, without interpolation or smoothing, with the same colours, classes and legend. Both styles are in the download package. Forecast values and statistics are unchanged.

releases.title: Method and references

changes.text: Methods section: new 'Method and references' panel naming the bias-correction method (per-cell mean–variance scaling), the probability and blending steps, the scores, and the scientific references with DOIs (checked on Crossref). Full text in docs/46. Forecasts and scores are unchanged.

releases.title: Bias correction section

changes.text: New 'Bias correction' section: benchmark of 13 rainfall-amount bias-correction methods against the operational mean-variance scaling for the September-initialized ONDJ cycle (data, method definitions, steps, results by target and region, gate statistics, figures, interpretation, downloads and references; docs/47). The published forecasts are unchanged.

releases.title: Bias correction: review revision (screening, confirmation, method fixes)

changes.text: Bias correction section revised after an external review: screening marks distinguish within-method and family-wide Holm adjustment ('screen_pass', not 'adopt'); a new selection-aware confirmation runs every method through the full probability pipeline with the blend weight fitted inside the folds; the test-period shortlist rule was removed.

Method fixes: Scaled Distribution Mapping follows the published steps (checked against an independent implementation); a documented dry-total and tie policy for the quantile-mapping methods; Variance Scaling uses the same fallback as MVS; DQM and QDM descriptions corrected; activation of limits and fallbacks reported.

Ordinary CRPS is the primary amount score (fair CRPS as a diagnostic); coverage, dry shares and run provenance added; the region switch is labelled as applying to the result tables, and the summary, interpretation and figures as national. The published forecasts are unchanged.

releases.title: Bias correction: review revision 3 (downloads, reproducibility, edge cases)

changes.text: Bias correction downloads: the per-cell scores and corrected forecast members (NetCDF) are now published; the site build checks that every advertised download and asset is deployable.

Reproducible reruns: one dependency fingerprint (configurations, masks, inputs, calculation code) validates checkpoints and is recorded as provenance. Fixes: configured smoothing in the confirmation, dry rule after EQM/DQM extrapolation, SDM rank order; results unchanged at the reported precision.

January amounts: the gains of square-root MVS and Gamma QM come almost entirely from cells that are wet in every training year; no cell of Ethiopia has 0 mm in every training year, so an all-zero guard for MVS (evaluated as a variant) never acts. The published forecasts are unchanged.

releases.title: Bias correction: all four cycles

changes.text: The bias-correction screening and confirmation now cover all cycles (January and February FMAM, May JJAS, September ONDJ), with a cycle picker in the Bias correction section. Published probabilities: MVS is not significantly beaten except for February in the February-initialized cycle, where square-root MVS is confirmed better. Amount gains are month-specific (ONDJ January, FMAM February-March, JJAS June-September). The published forecasts are unchanged.

releases.title: Bias correction: ratio-limit study and a shadow pilot

changes.text: MVS ratio-limit study for all cycles: wider spread-ratio limits do not change the published probabilities (at most 0.002 RPSS) and help rainfall amounts only in some months (JJAS July-September, ONDJ January, FMAM February-March for the January initialization), while lowering the ONDJ season's amount skill.

Shadow pilot of square-root MVS for February of the February-initialized FMAM cycle: reproduces the published February 2026 forecast with MVS, and scores the alternative against February 2026 (one season, an illustration). Not a published forecast; the published forecasts are unchanged.

releases.title: Shadow forecast, suggested methods and sortable tables

changes.text: Ongoing shadow forecast: square-root MVS for February of the February-initialized FMAM cycle runs automatically next to the published forecast in every such cycle and is scored once observed (never published as a forecast).

Suggested method for every cycle, target and product, from the historical CHIRPS confirmation and the independent validation seasons, by a rule fixed in advance. After 2026: candidates for February FMAM probabilities (square-root MVS), JJAS July-August amounts (VS) and ONDJ January amounts (square-root MVS); keep MVS elsewhere. The published forecasts are unchanged.
Every table on the site can be sorted by clicking a column header (numbers by value, text alphabetically; a third click restores the original order).

releases.title: Probability calibration, Phase 1

changes.text: New section 'Probability and rainfall-distribution calibration': Phase 1 benchmark of six tercile-probability methods (pseudocount smoothing, the incumbent climatology blend, temperature scaling, regularized Dirichlet calibration, multinomial and ordinal logistic regression) with the amount correction fixed, nested year-based validation and a selection-aware procedure, for all four cycles. No method is confirmed better than the incumbent blend; the published forecasts are unchanged.

releases.title: Probability calibration, Phase 2

changes.text: Phase 2 of the probability and rainfall-distribution calibration, for all four cycles: one-vs-rest binary calibrators (Platt, beta, isotonic) against the incumbent blend, and rainfall-distribution models from the raw ensemble (EMOS with a censored shifted gamma, extended logistic regression, quantile regression) scored for terciles, amounts (CRPS), quantiles and interval coverage. No method is confirmed better than the published probabilities. EMOS (January-initialized FMAM season; JJAS September) and quantile regression (JJAS September) are confirmed better than the MVS-corrected ensemble in CRPS, and the distribution models' 10-90% intervals are close to calibrated where the MVS ensemble's are too narrow. The published forecasts are unchanged.

releases.title: Amount and range shadow; downloads as release assets; new site pages

changes.text: Shadow rainfall-amount and range forecast (not published): every cycle also runs the EMOS distribution model and records each target's median and 10-90% range next to the MVS-corrected ensemble, scored once CHIRPS is available. 2026 so far (13 targets observed): the EMOS range is closer to calibrated coverage in 9 and has the higher CRPSS in 5; the MVS ensemble is clearly better in CRPS for JJAS June-August. The published forecasts are unchanged.
Probability calibration Phase 3 (Bayesian joint probability, BMA for precipitation, quantile regression forests) is implemented; its benchmark is running and the results follow in the next release.

Large download files (NetCDF, JSON, PDF, CSV) are served from the GitHub release 'site-files', named by their content so links never change; the site is half its former size. Every build also writes the site's data as JSON (site_data/), from which new pages are built: overview, probability calibration, bias correction, downloads and releases, under /next/ (docs/49).

releases.title: Probability calibration, Phase 3

changes.text: Phase 3 of the probability and rainfall-distribution calibration, for all four cycles: Bayesian joint probability, BMA for precipitation and quantile regression forests, scored for terciles, amounts (CRPS), quantiles and interval coverage. No model is confirmed better than the published probabilities or the MVS-corrected ensemble. BMA is the strongest (CRPSS above the MVS ensemble in 13 of 20 targets, none significant); BJP and BMA give near-calibrated 10-90% ranges (78-86%), the forest too narrow ones (69-76%). Across Phases 1-3, the incumbent climatology blend stays; EMOS remains the model of the amount and range shadow. The published forecasts are unchanged.

releases.title: Outlooks, maps and verification on the new pages; daily scoring of new observations

changes.text: The forecast outlooks, maps, verification and historical performance are on the new pages (/next/): one page per cycle, area and target with the map viewer and the official-outlook comparison, and per cycle and area the verification and the historical verification explorer. Their text was checked against the current page for every cycle, area and target.

New observations are checked daily and each season is scored as soon as its CHIRPS month is published (verification, official-outlook comparison, bias-correction validation, the amount and range shadow and the method suggestions); publishing the new scores stays a release step.

assets: site/assets (figures and maps, paths relative to the site root)
